reader_notes: Read from the note text, bars 1-52, with dump.ts for the whole piece and a throwaway comparison script to confirm the exchange at bars 5-6 and the tonic return at 44-47; every call was then checked by reading the passage. No published analysis was consulted. Beats are eighths. x = D E F G A Bb | C# Bb A G F E (1:1-2:3.5): a six-note rising scale, a drop of a diminished seventh to the leading tone, then a falling scale. y = the leader's eighth-note arpeggios against x in the bass, F A D | G C# E (3:1-4:3). x is used throughout in diatonic transpositions (e.g. starting on the third degree: F G A B C# D | E D C# B A G at 42) and with its first note changed (Bb G A Bb C D | E D ... at 11 and 40).

opening.leader_meanwhile: exchange: the leader plays y against x in the bass (3-4); then the leader takes x again an octave higher (5:1, D5) while the bass takes y (5:1 F3 A3 D4 | E3 G3 C#4): the two lines exchange at the octave
opening.notes: x is copied exactly (3:1-4:3.5). y in the bass is varied in its second bar: E3 G3 C#4 where the right hand had G4 C#5 E5 (the same diminished chord in another position, so that the bass does not lie a tritone below C#5). The imitation is not a canon: the bass's eighths from bar 7 are no longer the leader's.

Then the cadence (48).

Bass x in g (38:1 A3 A2 Bb2 C3 D3 Eb3 | F#2 Eb3 D3 C3 Bb2 A2, first note changed to A) against right-hand eighths ending in an arpeggio (39 D4 F#4 A4, like y's second bar); then x in the right hand in F (40:1 Bb4 G4 A4 Bb4 C5 D5 | E4 D5 C5 Bb4 A4 G4, first note changed) against bass eighths (G2 e. G2 A2 Bb2 | C2 G2 C3). The alternation of x between the voices against eighths reproduces alpha's exchange, but y is only partly present and the second statement is a step lower (F), not in the same key.

notes: Almost everything is made from x, in whole or as its rising or falling half, in sequences against eighth-note accompaniment or a held note. y appears only in the opening exchange and its tonic return (and in arpeggios like it at 7-10 and 26-27), so the exchange of x and y frames the piece rather than driving it. x is two bars of 3/8 (twelve sixteenths), longer than the protocol's half-bar motive; it is still treated as a motive (cut into halves, transposed diatonically, sequenced), which is why motivic-sequential is chosen over double. The two long pedals (C above x in 18-22, E below x in 29-34) are the clearest paired segments in the piece.
